question: The dataset provides only raw paired-end FASTQ reads (6 samples, not yet quantified) — no count matrix or abundance table exists yet. Producing gene-level counts for a treated-vs-control DE test requires a read aligner/pseudo-aligner (e.g., STAR, HISAT2, salmon, kallisto) or Rsubread's align()+featureCounts() workflow. I checked the sandbox's Python and R (CRAN/Bioconductor/GitHub) package inventories and none of these are installed: salmon, STAR, kallisto, tximport, subread, Rsubread, featureCounts, hisat2, bowtie2, Rhisat2, minimap2, bwa are all absent. A GENCODE v50 human GTF and a GRCh38.p13 FASTA (bundled for PharmCAT) are present as references, but there is no quantification tool available to turn the FASTQ reads into counts using them. Without one of these tools, I cannot plan a quantification step that would do anything but fail. Can you either (a) provide a pre-computed gene-level count matrix / transcript abundance table for these 6 liver samples instead of raw FASTQ, or (b) confirm a specific aligner/quantifier (STAR, salmon, kallisto, HISAT2, or Rsubread) that will be provisioned in the sandbox so I can plan the FASTQ-to-counts step against it?
